name: Color Banding & Quantization Analysis
description: Detects the abnormal presence of 'color banding' (posterization) and discrete quantization steps within smooth gradient regions (like skies or shadows). Generative AI models, especially Denoising Diffusion models, inherently operate within constrained numerical precision and latents, which often causes them to synthesize smooth surfaces with microscopic, stair-stepping color bands instead of the continuous analog light capture produced by genuine camera sensors.
mechanism: The algorithm isolates smooth regions in an image where color should mathematically transition continuously. It then traverses these regions, comparing adjacent pixel differences to locate discrete, artificial 'staircase' steps in pixel brightness. Real camera sensors capture light as continuous analog signals, naturally masking these steps with organic photon noise (dithering). AI generators, however, synthesize color values from highly compressed latent representations, frequently failing to seamlessly render smooth transitions, thereby leaving behind subtle, un-dithered quantized 'rings' or 'bands'.
parameters: Window Size: 5x5 pixels, Gradient Transition Target: 3-40 intensity levels, Step Detection Logic: Local differential > strict threshold
accuracy: Moderate (70-80%) - An extremely reliable flag when banding is discovered, but its standalone capability is heavily threatened by aggressively compressed authentic images that suffer from the exact same digital banding.
source: Farid (2009) / Wang (2004) - Image Quantization and Compression Forensics
useCase: Acting as an anomaly sniper to catch unnatural posterization in generated skies, skin, or smooth surfaces, exposing the mathematical precision limits of an AI model's latent space synthesis.

references.title: Wang, Z. et al. (2004). Image Quality Assessment: From Error Visibility to Structural Similarity. IEEE TIP.
Farid, H. (2009). Image Forgery Detection. IEEE Signal Processing Magazine.

strengths:
• Surgically precise at catching lazy AI generators that fail to properly dither smooth transitions.
• Identifies hard mathematical precision limitations in AI decoders (like VAEs used in Stable Diffusion).
• Extremely fast and lightweight, requiring minimal compute to calculate local luminance derivatives.
limitations:
• Extreme vulnerability to false positives: Authentic photos saved hastily in low-quality JPEG or subjected to fierce network compression (WhatsApp/Messenger) will naturally develop the exact same banding.
• Some advanced diffusion models or prompt engineers specifically inject 'film grain' or digital noise to artificially mask and dither these bands, blinding the algorithm.
• Completely blind and useless on high-frequency, complex textures (like grass, gravel, or foliage) where no smooth gradients exist.
